body: Did anything change at all on the CI machines? I find it quite strange that "heavy load" has become a problem only now and is triggering this problem so frequently when we never saw it in the past.

@jmmv It's very hard to say. We upgraded the production fleet to macOS Catalina on 2020-01-29 (but on testing CI already much earlier, I think since the beta), and the test worked fine until yesterday. I remember seeing the same failure occasionally during a presubmit of my CL in the testing org, but that was a completely unrelated change, then it went away a few days later and I was able to submit it.

Maybe it's a bug in macOS Catalina, but it's not clear what triggers it :|

Alright, I think I know what happens. The test starts by doing:

```java
View view1 = underTest.getCurrentView(watchFsEnabledProvider);
```

which in turn calls `MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwareness#init` to initialize the monitor. But the monitor is started in a separate thread. There is no guarantee that by the end of init, fsevents is already listening for changes, so if the thread is delayed, we can modify the client before fsevents starts to listen -- and thus we lose the initial events and we don't see anything ever changing.

Trivial to expose this by adding a sleep right before the call to `MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwareness#run`.
Haha, and of course not yet fixed. Flaked again.

I spent a lot of time on the theory that this is caused by heavy machine load but could not trigger a single problem on various machines (including an iMac Pro as BazelCI uses) by running the test hundreds of times while, at the same time, running a very large build in the background. I even "reniced" `fseventsd` to 20 to try to make it slower, but that had no effect either.

So I ended up writing a test that creates files concurrently from a bunch of threads (100 threads, 50 files each). This is not "load" in the sense as I was looking for earlier given that this completes in milliseconds and `fseventsd` barely uses any CPU. But bingo. Our diff awareness code is almost always failing to reliably detect all notifications. Use 1 thread and 5000 files and things work though, so it's not necessarily the number of files to monitor that's the problem.

Digging further, and reading through the `FSEvents.h` header (which is much more completely documented than the online documentation for some reason)... I encountered `kFSEventStreamEventFlagMustScanSubDirs`, which tells the caller that they are responsible for looking for further changes as events may have dropped. And lo and behold, if we look into the flags we get in `FsEventsDiffAwarenessCallback` when the test fails, we are being told about this condition. Further, we are told `kFSEventStreamEventFlagUserDropped`, which means we aren't processing events fast enough and they drop because of us.

In other words, our usage of the `FSEvents` API is incorrect and we are missing changes when we can't keep up with the notifications. We must interpret these flags to know when events dropped and do something about them. I guess the easiest solution on this condition is to "give up" and assume "everything changed" in the response. Looking into it.

cc @haxorz

Our good old friend is back again: Always failing with this: ``` There was 1 failure: 1) testSimple(com.google.devtools.build.lib.skyframe.MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwarenessTest) java.lang.AssertionError: Paths [b/c/d, a, b, a/b, a/b/c, b/c] not found as modified at com.google.devtools.build.lib.skyframe.MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwarenessTest.assertDiff(MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwarenessTest.java:144) at com.google.devtools.build.lib.skyframe.MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwarenessTest.testSimple(MacOSXFsEventsDiffAwarenessTest.java:161) ``` I'm disabling the test again. 😭

To make things worse, `testStress` gets stuck if run with `--runs_per_test` over about 10 because we end up with too many concurrent threads opening files and, I think, running into process limits without good error control. But still cannot reproduce the flakiness issues.
